+unchanged numerical/envelope/token values in actual caller and consumer checks.

+independent reviewers must inspect the actual immutable candidate. No human
+numerical/legal signoff, publication authority or Astrofolio integration follows.

+# C-014 normal-page evidence audit
+
+Accepted for the stated finite local-page scope. **The evidence contains 24 accepted groups from two executions**: the first run's 12 Moon groups and the corrected second run's 12 Chart groups. The first run remains failed, with all 12 original Chart failures preserved. This audit did not run another browser or alter product files.
+
+Each original Chart failure occurred at the same `error.count() === 0` assertion after editing the refused date to December 31. Its captured state has the retained localized error, cleared result/actions/context, and focus on `birth-date`. Independent source review confirms that ordinary Chart date edits clear field validation and results but retain the separate calculation error; non-busy submission clears it before calculation. Moon explicitly clears its error on edit. Eighteen complete source paths and two run prefixes are unchanged by C-014, and the relevant islands/BirthFields are unchanged by C-012. The corrected driver changes only its qualification, affected Chart-only scope/count, and this pre-retry assertion: it checks retained error and date focus before verifying error-free successful recovery. It does not weaken the refusal or successful-result checks.
+
+I independently reconciled all 36 per-case JSON records with their aggregates, rehashed their 72 screenshots, verified both driver identities and the correction diff, and reconstructed the accepted locale/tool/width set: EN/ES/FR/IT/PT/RU × Chart/Moon × 1280/390. Each accepted group records ordinary unknown-time Apia on December 29, prior-result clearing on edit, focused dedicated refusal for December 30, and successful December 31 recovery. Two EN/1280 controls preserve explicit 08:30 calculations on December 30. Actual built GeoNames selection remains Apia, Tuamasaga, Samoa, Pacific/Apia. The drivers use actual local normal-build pages and native form/city controls; they do not replace engine, resolver, component, loader or request-response data.
+
+Both runs record Node 22.23.2 and Chrome 152.0.7977.83, HEAD `3845a04bcea822da3c30a18848ef3d8d133b7b66` plus the explicitly recorded working C-014 changes, and freeze identity `328ea15bd192573894639dab699058cb83185e0c61e907dde7f275305cfe48c2`. All 18 source identities agree before/after both runs and with files rehashed during this audit; the original 12 frozen files match exactly. All 108 served files common to both runs have identical bytes; all 131 unique served files also match the current normal dist at audit time. The independent source audit preserves exact Git/base/frozen/root captures and reconstructs the three source-proof snippets.
+
+Across the 24 accepted groups there are 24 expected generic refusal console errors; across all 36 executions there are 36. None exposes native formatter details. Both executions retain zero unexpected console errors, uncaught page errors, request failures, blocked requests or non-GET requests. All states sampled for accepted refusal/recovery have no saved profile and no horizontal overflow. The drivers close their browser contexts, browser and static server. Request observations and static-server response records do not imply every browser request completed or exercise Plausible delivery.
+
+The 18 final release-capture files rehash to their recorded prior/current equal hashes; the linked build receipt records template source `e664d1d35eeae647eff10cc775f058d16e179bea4f0006313a91f3f0d4a3b3b7`. The root's separate visual inspection of RU Chart mobile and FR Moon mobile is attributed to the root, not this audit. I did not rerun or independently certify the full test/build gates here.
+
+This is an evidence and source audit of the root's actual local browser executions. It does not certify numerical call counts, an independent numerical oracle, an empty date, complete local-date or Sun/Moon candidate coverage, signed-in lifecycle, remote preview, publication or production deployment. The missing membership witness remains an inability to calculate a reference, not proof that the date is empty. `audit-result.json`, the original-input manifest, immutable copied drivers/results/correction and the child's source review support these conclusions. Original screenshot binaries remain in the root run directories; their exact identities are preserved without duplicating them in this supplemental delivery.

+# C-014 normal-page harness: independent source audit
+
+The correction rationale is supported by the actual source. After a settled refusal, **an ordinary Chart date edit retains the calculation error until a subsequent non-busy submission clears it; Moon clears its error on the edit itself**. This difference predates C-014 and C-012. The dedicated C-014 refusal message is new; its error-state lifetime follows the existing handlers. No source mismatch was found.
+
+The captured root HEAD is `3845a04bcea822da3c30a18848ef3d8d133b7b66`. Its working ChartCalculator and MoonPhaseTool bytes match the twelve-file C-014 freeze exactly: Chart SHA-256 `b1e293351add28ece576d95ccfec5fb84a54bc92097528076acfb78da02dc263`, Moon `7ce6b5683b7d00c4aa1bfc9aeee1d0de593b500df55b988690cb2062a8f5730f`. Source captures include both pre-C012 `c7b9eb4…` and post-C012 `3845a04b…` versions, frozen files and actual root files.
+
+- Chart's `BirthFields` date input delegates through `onDateChange` (BirthFields line 63). The Chart callback (lines 1807–1811) calls `invalidateProfileHandoff()`, sets the date, and clears **fieldErrors.date**, a separate state from `error`. The invalidation path (496–504), `advanceInputRevision` (401–405), `clearResult` (418–445), and their local clearing helpers contain no `setError` call. Result/actions/context clear without clearing that alert.
+- Chart `compute` (1320–1356) returns early while busy; otherwise it sets `error` to an empty string at line 1330 before returning for incomplete fields or starting a new calculation. `runChart` independently clears it at line 1156 before its first awaited load. A valid successful retry therefore has no previous alert. This does not claim that every submission succeeds or that an incomplete form bypasses validation.
+- Moon's date callback (221–224) calls `invalidateLookup` (91–97), which explicitly clears `error` at line 95. Its time and place handlers use the same path. `lookup` also clears error at line 107 after the nonempty-date guard. The Chart and Moon handlers should therefore not share an assertion that the alert disappears immediately on edit.
+
+The AST/byte comparison independently proves equality of all eighteen relevant complete functions, callbacks and focus effects between the actual root files and the exact pre-C014 base. The two run-start statement sequences also match after omitting only C-014's new local error-sentinel declaration. C-014's retained diff changes imports, the unknown-time witness admission and error selection, not these edit/reset paths. C-012 changes neither island nor BirthFields at all (the retained three-file `c7…3845` diff is empty). Its new synchronous context-clear event affects the separate daily panel and capture surfaces; the captured listeners do not clear Chart's calculation error.
+
+Chart invalidation sets `focusAfterComputeRef.current = false`; the unchanged post-compute focus effect (1117–1128) returns when that flag is false. The source therefore does not request error focus again on this ordinary edit. Actual browser focus, output visibility, request counts and the parent's 24 accepted native groups remain the parent's runtime evidence, not claims from this source-only audit. A separate primary-profile revocation explicitly clears Chart error at line 487, so “until retry” is qualified to the ordinary date-edit flow, not every possible event.
+
+All three `sourceProof` hashes in `normal-chart-harness-correction.json` are reproducible. The first two cover the indented function through one following newline; the `invalidateProfileHandoff` hash includes two following newlines. The initial four common span definitions reproduced two hashes; the retained bounded exact-span lookup identified the third's trailing blank line, and the final AST record includes that exact definition. This is a snippet-boundary difference, not a source discrepancy.
+
+This audit executed no browser run, product code or new product tests. It captured source, compared immutable Git/file bytes and parsed TypeScript ASTs. No root/author/product/shared-document edits occurred. The recorded command/parser output, exact source identities and excerpts are copy-ready evidence; the main reviewer owns reconciliation of the original and corrected normal-page runs.

+name: Site Check
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+  # Stacked packet PRs target the preceding packet branch, so every PR base
+  # must receive the same regression gates as main.
+  pull_request:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      scope_base:
+        description: Commit SHA or ref to compare for the protected-scope guard
+        required: true
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  build-check:
+    name: Build & Check
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Node
+        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+          cache: npm
+
+      - name: Phase 1 protected-scope guard
+        env:
+          PHASE1_SCOPE_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.scope_base || github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
+        run: npm run test:phase1:scope
+
+      - name: Install
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Dependency advisories stay at zero
+        # Production tree must be clean at any severity; the full tree
+        # (dev included) fails only on high/critical so a low-severity
+        # transitive dev advisory cannot block an unrelated deploy.
+        # Retry only recognized, findings-free audit endpoint outages;
+        # every other failure and exhausted retries remain fatal.
+        run: |
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --omit=dev
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --audit-level=high
+
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: npx playwright-core install chromium
+
+      - name: Validate registry JSON
+        run: node -e "JSON.parse(require('node:fs').readFileSync('public/registry/zodiacs.registry.json', 'utf8'))"
+
+      - name: Check for stale repo or bridge wording
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RInE 'Symbiosis|ZodiacS(DK)|diasmal[[:digit:]]{3}|zodiacs-org/sdk' public/sdk public/registry README.md CLAUDE.md DESIGNER_HANDOFF.md
+
+      - name: Wing language stays in the wing
+        # The source-aware gate checks rendered strings across Astro, TS/TSX,
+        # MDX, JSON, email/share code, and API output. Legal and Registry
+        # carve-outs are exact and tested; arbitrary directory bypasses are not.
+        run: npm run check:consumer-boundary
+
+      - name: Voice — banned tells stay out of the copy
+        # The smug vocabulary CLAUDE.md bans on new surfaces, enforced
+        # over every content file and template the agents touch.
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RIniE 'done properly|computed properly|shows? (its|their) work|like a human( wrote it)?|no mush|not vibes|speaks human|in plain language|como es debido|sin paja' src/content src/pages src/components src/islands
+
+      - name: Authorship stays transparent
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RInE 'Rowan Vale|about/#editor([^i]|$)|"@type"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"Person"' src
+
+      - name: Verify daily editorial package
+        run: npm run editorial:daily:verify
+
+      - name: Replay 30 daily editions
+        run: npm run editorial:daily:replay
+
+      - name: Build
+        run: npm run build
+
+      - name: Typecheck
+        run: npm run check
+
+      - name: Thesis reading and evidence at six viewport widths
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/thesis npm run test:thesis:browser
+
+      - name: Upload thesis screenshots
+        if: always()
+        uses: actions/upload-artifact@ea165f8d65b6e75b540449e92b4886f43607fa02 # v4.6.2
+        with:
+          name: thesis-browser-${{ github.run_id }}
+          path: tests/visual/artifacts/thesis/
+          if-no-files-found: ignore
+          retention-days: 30
+
+      - name: Birth chart export and sharing acceptance
+        env:
+          T17_SHARE_EVIDENCE: "1"
+        run: node tests/t17-positions-share.mjs
+
+      - name: Imported calendar input boundaries
+        run: node tests/platform-share-boundary-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Moon lookup result ownership
+        timeout-minutes: 3
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/moon-result-ownership node tests/moon-result-ownership-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Birth chart result ownership
+        timeout-minutes: 5
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/chart-ownership node tests/chart-ownership-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Chart-linked prompt result ownership
+        timeout-minutes: 5
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/post-chart-context-clear node tests/post-chart-context-clear-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Unknown-time local date reference
+        timeout-minutes: 5
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/local-date-reference node tests/local-date-reference-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Engine accuracy vectors
+        run: npm test
+
+      - name: Platform starter fresh consumer
+        timeout-minutes: 6
+        run: node scripts/verify-platform-starter.mjs --install
+
+      - name: Phase 1 exact-width acceptance evidence
+        run: npm run test:phase1:evidence
+
+      - name: Weekly digest smoke
+        run: npm run digest:weekly -- --dry-run --fixture --week-start 2026-07-13 --limit 1
+
+      - name: Link & artifact integrity over dist
+        run: node scripts/check-dist.mjs
+
+      - name: I18n route-boundary regression
+        run: npm run test:i18n:r0
+
+      - name: Russian R2 public-locale acceptance
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/i18n-r2-ru npm run test:i18n:r2
+
+      - name: Homepage poster motion and deferred video
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/home-hero npm run test:home-hero:browser
+
+      - name: Homepage interactive chart preview
+        run: npm run test:home-demo:browser
+
+      - name: Phase 2 sky-events publication drive
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/events npm run test:events:browser
+
+      - name: Phase 5 People noindex pilot
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/phase5-people npm run test:phase5:people
+
+      - name: Phase 6 Ask Zodiacs drive
+        run: npm run test:phase6:ask
+
+      - name: Today SSR and personalization
+        run: npm run test:today:browser
+
+      - name: Horoscope templates, SSR, and responsive behavior
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/horoscope-program npm run test:horoscopes:browser
+
+      - name: Link-in-bio page acceptance
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/bio npm run test:bio:browser
+
+      - name: Existing compatibility regression drive
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/compatibility npm run test:compatibility:browser
+
+      - name: Existing Registry selector regression drive
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/registry npm run test:registry-selector:browser
+
+      - name: Zodiac Markets mobile terminal acceptance
+        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/zodiac-markets node tests/registry-exchange-mobile-drive.mjs
+
+      - name: Phase 1 mobile frame cadence
+        run: npm run test:phase1:frames
+
+      - name: Structured data validation
+        run: npm run schema:check
+
+      - name: Bundle size & engine isolation gates
+        run: node scripts/report-bundles.mjs --fail
+
+      - name: Visual regression
+        run: npm run test:visual
+
+      - name: Lighthouse performance budgets
+        run: npm run test:lighthouse
+
+      - name: Foreign-origin widget integration
+        run: npm run test:widgets:browser
+

+from pathlib import Path
+import collections
+import datetime
+import hashlib
+import json
+import subprocess
+
+ROOT = Path('/Users/chiburashka/.codex/worktrees/4806/site')
+OUT = Path(__file__).parent
+HEAD = 'f803d2543ad81343b22d49326b8b46d0e2ea03a0'
+BASE = '3845a04bcea822da3c30a18848ef3d8d133b7b66'
+def git(*args):
+    return subprocess.check_output(['git', *args], cwd=ROOT)
+def sha(data):
+    return hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()
+def dump(path, value):
+    (OUT / path).write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2) + '\n')
+def save(path, data):
+    dest = OUT / path
+    dest.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
+    dest.write_bytes(data)
+
+before = json.loads((OUT / 'pr-before.json').read_text())
+after = json.loads((OUT / 'pr-after.json').read_text())
+for p in (before, after):
+    assert (p['number'], p['state'], p['draft']) == (435, 'open', True)
+    assert p['head']['sha'] == HEAD and p['base']['sha'] == BASE
+    assert p['head']['repo']['full_name'] == p['base']['repo']['full_name'] == 'ZodiacsOfficial/site'
+assert before['title'] == after['title']
+assert before['changed_files'] == after['changed_files']
+pages = json.loads((OUT / 'files-pages.json').read_text())
+remote = sum(pages, [])
+assert len(remote) == before['changed_files'] == 314
+assert all(len(p) == 100 for p in pages[:-1]) and len(pages[-1]) == 14
+assert len({r['filename'] for r in remote}) == len(remote)
+merge = git('merge-base', BASE, HEAD).decode().strip()
+assert merge == BASE
+save('local-commit.txt', git('show', '-s', '--format=fuller', HEAD))
+save('local-base.txt', git('show', '-s', '--format=fuller', BASE))
+save('local-merge-base.txt', (merge + '\n').encode())
+
+def tree(ref):
+    value = {}
+    for record in git('ls-tree', '-r', '-z', ref).split(b'\0'):
+        if not record:
+            continue
+        header, name = record.split(b'\t', 1)
+        mode, kind, blob = header.decode().split()
+        value[name.decode()] = dict(mode=mode, kind=kind, sha=blob)
+    return value
+head_tree, base_tree = tree(HEAD), tree(BASE)
+raw_status = git('diff', '--name-status', '-z', '--find-renames', BASE + '...' + HEAD)
+save('local-name-status.raw', raw_status)
+parts = [x.decode() for x in raw_status.split(b'\0') if x]
+statuses, i = {}, 0
+while i < len(parts):
+    code = parts[i]
+    i += 1
+    if code.startswith(('R', 'C')):
+        previous, name = parts[i:i+2]
+        i += 2
+    else:
+        name, previous = parts[i], None
+        i += 1
+    statuses[name] = {'code': code, 'previous': previous}
+assert set(statuses) == {r['filename'] for r in remote}
+
+records = []
+for r in remote:
+    name = r['filename']
+    local = head_tree.get(name)
+    # The actual diff contains additions and modifications only. Fail on expansion.
+    assert r['status'] in ('added', 'modified')
+    assert statuses[name]['code'] == {'added': 'A', 'modified': 'M'}[r['status']]
+    assert local and local['kind'] == 'blob' and local['sha'] == r['sha']
+    data = git('cat-file', 'blob', local['sha'])
+    recomputed_blob = hashlib.sha1(b'blob ' + str(len(data)).encode() + b'\0' + data).hexdigest()
+    assert recomputed_blob == r['sha']
+    records.append({'path': name, 'status': r['status'], 'localStatus': statuses[name]['code'],
+                    'remoteBlob': r['sha'], 'localBlob': local['sha'], 'recomputedBlob': recomputed_blob,
+                    'sha256': sha(data), 'bytes': len(data), 'mode': local['mode'],
+                    'isDocumentationPath': name.startswith('docs/'), 'verified': True})
+dump('changed-file-identities.json', records)
+
+freeze_inputs = [
+    ('c014-source-freeze.json', Path('/private/tmp/zodiacs-platform-local-date-reference-evidence/source-freeze.json'),
+     '328ea15bd192573894639dab699058cb83185e0c61e907dde7f275305cfe48c2'),
+    ('supplement-identity.json', Path('/private/tmp/zodiacs-platform-local-date-catalog-count-integration/identity.json'), None)
+]
+patch_source = Path('/private/tmp/zodiacs-platform-local-date-catalog-count-integration/integration.patch').read_bytes()
+assert sha(patch_source) == '50330a5cc5865f44872f607795b1135bf5c98a0a1ffd06113ccf6cfcebff5922'
+save('integration.patch', patch_source)
+frozen, frozen_paths = [], set()
+for label, source, expected_manifest in freeze_inputs:
+    data = source.read_bytes()
+    if expected_manifest:
+        assert sha(data) == expected_manifest
+    save(label, data)
+    identity = json.loads(data)
+    for item in identity.get('files', identity.get('records')):
+        name = item['path']
+        actual = git('show', HEAD + ':' + name)
+        assert sha(actual) == item['sha256'] and len(actual) == item['bytes']
+        assert name not in frozen_paths
+        frozen_paths.add(name)
+        save('source/' + name, actual)
+        frozen.append({'path': name, 'identitySource': label, 'expectedSha256': item['sha256'],
+                       'actualSha256': sha(actual), 'bytes': len(actual),
+                       'gitBlob': head_tree[name]['sha'], 'verified': True})
+workflow = '.github/workflows/site-check.yml'
+non_docs = [r for r in records if not r['isDocumentationPath']]
+assert {r['path'] for r in non_docs} == frozen_paths | {workflow}
+assert len(frozen) == 16 and len(non_docs) == 16
+workflow_base = git('show', BASE + ':' + workflow)
+workflow_head = git('show', HEAD + ':' + workflow)
+addition = (
+    b'      - name: Unknown-time local date reference\n'
+    b'        timeout-minutes: 5\n'
+    b'        run: OUT_DIR=tests/visual/artifacts/local-date-reference node tests/local-date-reference-drive.mjs\n\n'
+)
+anchor = b'      - name: Engine accuracy vectors\n'

+name: Site Check
+
+on:
+  push:
+    branches:
+      - main
+  # Stacked packet PRs target the preceding packet branch, so every PR base
+  # must receive the same regression gates as main.
+  pull_request:
+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:
+      scope_base:
+        description: Commit SHA or ref to compare for the protected-scope guard
+        required: true
+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
+jobs:
+  build-check:
+    name: Build & Check
+    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout
+        uses: actions/checkout@d23441a48e516b6c34aea4fa41551a30e30af803 # v6.1.0
+        with:
+          fetch-depth: 0
+
+      - name: Setup Node
+        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+          cache: npm
+
+      - name: Phase 1 protected-scope guard
+        env:
+          PHASE1_SCOPE_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.scope_base || github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
+        run: npm run test:phase1:scope
+
+      - name: Install
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Dependency advisories stay at zero
+        # Production tree must be clean at any severity; the full tree
+        # (dev included) fails only on high/critical so a low-severity
+        # transitive dev advisory cannot block an unrelated deploy.
+        # Retry only recognized, findings-free audit endpoint outages;
+        # every other failure and exhausted retries remain fatal.
+        run: |
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --omit=dev
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --audit-level=high
+
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: npx playwright-core install chromium
+
+      - name: Validate registry JSON
+        run: node -e "JSON.parse(require('node:fs').readFileSync('public/registry/zodiacs.registry.json', 'utf8'))"
+
+      - name: Check for stale repo or bridge wording
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RInE 'Symbiosis|ZodiacS(DK)|diasmal[[:digit:]]{3}|zodiacs-org/sdk' public/sdk public/registry README.md CLAUDE.md DESIGNER_HANDOFF.md

+        # MDX, JSON, email/share code, and API output. Legal and Registry
+        # carve-outs are exact and tested; arbitrary directory bypasses are not.

+
+      - name: Voice — banned tells stay out of the copy

+        # over every content file and template the agents touch.
+        run: |

+
+      - name: Authorship stays transparent
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RInE 'Rowan Vale|about/#editor([^i]|$)|"@type"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*"Person"' src
+
+      - name: Verify daily editorial package
+        run: npm run editorial:daily:verify
+
+      - name: Replay 30 daily editions

+
+      - name: Build

+# C-015 Chart reference confidence — author Freeze2
+
+The Chart caller now preserves its admitted reference calculation while leaving the Moon’s possible signs across an unknown birth time unverified. It sets the existing `moonSignCandidates` field to an empty array before signature/share preparation and uses the existing unresolved-confidence path. The singular Registry Sun bridge is retained only for known-time calculations. No false Sun claim was observed; this removal is a conservative response to missing date-wide coverage proof.
+
+**Frozen source:** base `f803d2543ad81343b22d49326b8b46d0e2ea03a0`, 16 files. `freeze2-identity.json` SHA256 `54cd5acbc7f69c7b3935943a9380be10bb18e8ca2b5a90c1d1766625d8bca55c`; `freeze2.patch` SHA256 `b13527901ee962d462b0ddd2bdbc16f82763ffa8ad7486d797358b46f76fd0a4`.

Eight test/driver files cover the actual caller, consumers, Registry/ownership behavior, key counts, sharing and the former endpoint-call expectation. Removing the added locale line restores every original catalog byte. A TypeScript AST comparison proves chart-date-certainty executable code unchanged. No SDK, endpoint algorithm, schema, account format, MoonPhaseTool, global styles, navigation, Registry/Astrofolio source or root documentation changes are included.
+
+## Observed behavior and exact preservation
+
+The native driver uses the actual Preact caller, actual rc.6 calculation/receipt modules, controlled synthetic city selection and loader/call observation. Its optional baseline overlays only the exact delivered f803 ChartCalculator. Shared numerical/receipt code is unchanged. The controlled coordinates are synthetic; the historical timezone/date membership and geocentric body values are real engine/Intl outputs.
+
+Six same-Chrome unknown-time comparisons preserve the exact native Chart JSON, compact numerical chart JSON after removing only the intentionally changed candidate metadata, immutable envelope JSON, actual downloaded receipt bytes and positions token. Toronto, Juneau, an ordinary singleton date, an ordinary two-sign date, a non-hour gap date and repeated Apia are covered. Known-time full/Moon/Rising paths also retain their exact own-path outputs and Registry behavior. Full mode executes its one public natal path; Moon/Rising retain their existing one legacy natal path. The former Chart endpoint-confidence calls are absent; this does not mean the primary calculation performs no ephemeris work.
+
+Concrete counterexamples remain visible in `native-summary.json` and the complete reports:
+
+- Toronto 1919-03-31: the previous `[aries]` claim omitted the member instant 1919-03-31T04:30Z, whose Moon is Pisces (Chrome longitude 359.7145003582242°). The result now carries `[]`.
+- Juneau 1867-10-18: the previous `[gemini]` claim omitted the returned-date member 1867-10-19T00:31:13Z, whose Moon is Cancer (97.12696569323725°). The result now carries `[]`.
+- Ordinary Bangkok and London controls deliberately also withhold a verified range: endpoint agreement or disagreement alone is no longer promoted to date-wide evidence. No wider sampling/completeness assertion is introduced.
+
+Actual consumer checks confirm unresolved Moon context, no definitive Moon approach/communication advice, no Moon communication aspects, existing signature filtering, scene propagation and unverified sharing labels. Positions wire bytes remain unchanged; the receiver’s existing `angles:null` rule keeps Moon confidence unresolved without adding a schema field. Actual normal-build sharing checks retain the Moon image/dialog uncertainty label, existing possibility warning and reference-position export behavior. Existing reference Sun values in post-chart events/context and save-related context are explicitly unchanged; disabling the Registry bridge is not whole-product Sun verification.
+

Existing layout/classes are retained. C014 refused dates still fail before numerical/receipt/endpoint work; recovery and typed fields/focus work. +# Independent C015 Freeze2 consumer review
+
+Accepted within the reviewed consumer, finite historical-control, and copy scope. No blocker found. This is separate from the main reviewer's actual ChartCalculator browser/save/receipt/ownership review and from the root metadata proposal review.
+
+## Exact source
+
+Base f803d2543ad81343b22d49326b8b46d0e2ea03a0. Author identity SHA256 54cd5acbc7f69c7b3935943a9380be10bb18e8ca2b5a90c1d1766625d8bca55c; patch b13527901ee962d462b0ddd2bdbc16f82763ffa8ad7486d797358b46f76fd0a4. All 16 author files were copied and verified in an independent checkout. Candidate ChartCalculator SHA256 188ccf4759f5586d832751be1de888d8f2d204a267bd5eaa1cf1823dd6c73475.
+
+The executable probe uses an exact contiguous TypeScript-AST-bounded span from candidate ChartCalculator lines 1201–1212 and baseline lines 1202–1220. Inside that span no statement is rewritten. The wrapper supplies the existing real engine/helper functions, records endpoint calls, and fixes runIsCurrent to true. It exercises the actual confidence decision; it does not execute the whole component or its asynchronous ownership checks. Extraction boundaries, source/span/wrapper hashes and both source versions are retained.
+
+## Executed checks
+
+Node 22.23.2 / ICU 78.2 / tz 2026a and Node 24.19.0 / ICU 78.3 / tz 2026b both passed four unknown-time controls (Toronto, Juneau, ordinary Bangkok and the old two-candidate London date) plus two supplied-time positive controls. Every unknown-time candidate produced empty Moon candidates, uncertainty true, a null Registry slug, and zero endpoint/body-sampling calls within the extracted confidence span. The baseline used three calls (one endpoint helper and two body samples). Known-time controls leave the full chart object unchanged, keep the reference Sun slug, and do not perform endpoint work.
+
+Actual unchanged consumer helpers produce unresolved Moon chart context with no sign, house or dignities; approach and communication withhold Moon advice; communication and signature omit Moon aspects; share-card models omit the definite Moon slug. No numerical longitude is moved. Existing numerical JSON, portable envelope string, positions token and saved-schema-shaped projection comparisons also pass, but these are direct calls/projections, not a persisted-save claim.
+
+Four actual Preact components were server-rendered from the frozen-branch results: Inspector (Moon selected), ChartShareDialog (Moon mode), ReadingPath, and PositionsOnlyResult. The 32 distinct baseline/candidate HTML artifacts reproduce with identical hashes on both runtimes. Candidate Inspector and share dialog show Needs a birth time and omit the definite Moon interpretation/glyph. ReadingPath offers no Moon-sign reading links and omits the supplied Moon-aspect and unverified ten-body totals. The positions receiver remains uncertain, including baseline controls; its existing protocol does not transport Moon-candidate metadata. Baseline singleton controls really render Moon interpretation and glyphs, establishing meaningful positive controls rather than only searching candidate omissions.
+
+Twenty-four additional source/artifact checks passed; eight signature/context checks passed. All 102 compiled input hashes were rechecked. Of these, 85 are site sources; all consumed executable consumer sources match base byte-for-byte except the exact new catalog entries and the endpoint helper's comments. Its executable AST is unchanged. The source/build/input manifests and raw logs are retained.
+
+## Finite historical counterexamples
+
+| Local date and zone | Old endpoint candidates | Actual member omitted by those candidates |
+| --- | --- | --- |
+| 1919-03-31, America/Toronto | Aries | 1919-03-31T04:30:00.000Z = local 00:30:00.000; Moon 359.7145003582242°, Pisces |
+| 1867-10-18, America/Juneau | Gemini | 1867-10-19T00:31:13.000Z = local Oct 18 15:33:32.000; Moon 97.12696569323725°, Cancer |
+
+Both runtimes agree on those inputs. The actual local-date membership helper admits each witness and rejects the immediately preceding millisecond (Toronto's prior date; Juneau's next date). These prove particular omissions, not a complete civil-date interval or an independent ephemeris accuracy oracle. The reference instants are still members. The Toronto signature changes from Moon trine Neptune to Mercury trine Saturn when its unverified Moon is withheld; Juneau's Mercury trine Uranus signature remains. Ordinary Bangkok changes from Sun sextile Moon to Sun trine Saturn. That conservative loss of a reading on an ordinary date is intentional policy, not a discovered crossing. What it represents

The Moon represents emotional needs, instinctive reactions, memory, and what helps you feel safe.

How the sign shapes it

In Scorpio, it takes on a fixed water style. Intense, private, all-or-nothing.

A birth time is needed to place it in a house, so this chart cannot say which area of life carries it.

Why it matters here

Scorpio shapes your emotional needs and instincts; The missing birth time means the life area remains open. It describes a tendency, not a guarantee of what will happen.

+export function normalizeContextTerm(value: string): string {
+  return value
+    .trim()
+    .toLowerCase()
+    .replace(/[’']/g, '')
+    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-')
+    .replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');

+
+const contextTermsByKey = new Map<string, ContextTermMetadata>();
+for (const entry of CONTEXT_TERMS) {

+  for (const alias of entry.aliases ?? []) {
+    contextTermsByKey.set(normalizeContextTerm(alias), entry);

+}

+export function resolveContextTerm(value: string): ContextTermMetadata | undefined {
+  return contextTermsByKey.get(normalizeContextTerm(value));

+/**
+ * Privacy-bounded product analytics.
+ *
+ * Only event names and properties declared here may leave the browser. The
+ * allowlist deliberately excludes URLs, addresses, email values, chart data,
+ * birth details, free text, and persistent identifiers.
+ */
+import {
+  ANALYTICS_EVENT_PROPS as EVENT_PROPS,
+  ANALYTICS_EVENT_VALUES as EVENT_VALUES,
+} from './analytics-config.mjs';
+
+export const ANALYTICS_EVENT_PROPS = EVENT_PROPS as Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>;
+export const ANALYTICS_EVENT_VALUES = EVENT_VALUES as Readonly<
+  Record<string, Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>>
+>;
+
+export type AnalyticsEventName =
+  | 'chart_computed'
+  | 'chart_saved'
+  | 'compat_computed'
+  | 'email_subscribed'
+  | 'share_card_downloaded'
+  | 'widget_embed_copied'
+  | 'registry_visit'
+  | 'registry_bridge_impression'
+  | 'registry_bridge_click'
+  | 'verifier_used'
+  | 'terminal_view_switch'
+  | 'sdk_click'
+  | 'bio_click'
+  | 'wallet_chart_computed'
+  | 'aura_view'
+  | 'aura_compose'
+  | 'aura_share'
+  | 'aura_refresh'
+  | 'aura_calculator'
+  | 'aura_entry'
+  | 'aura_return'
+  | 'aura_response'
+  | 'aura_cabinet_select'
+  | 'aura_cabinet_reveal'
+  | 'aura_talisman_personalize'
+  | 'invite_created'
+  | 'invite_opened'
+  | 'invite_completed'
+  | 'invite_returned'
+  | 'invite_converted'
+  | 'invite_revoked'
+  | 'result_rendered'
+  | 'explorer_interaction'
+  | 'tour_start'
+  | 'tour_complete'
+  | 'tour_step'
+  | 'context_help_opened'
+  | 'first_reading_prompt'
+  | 'first_reading_step'
+  | 'first_reading_completed'
+  | 'next_action_clicked'
+  | 'email_capture_viewed'
+  | 'search_open'
+  | 'search_go'
+  | 'assistant_open'

+  | 'push_prompt'

+  | 'today_view'
+  | 'living_chart_open'
+  | 'living_chart_saved'
+  | 'living_chart_deleted'
+  | 'living_chart_export'
+  | 'calendar_subscribe'
+  | 'chart_save'
+  | 'chart_share'
+  | 'wing_entry'
+  | 'lens_change'
+  | 'transit_search'
+  | 'srchart_view'
+  | 'composite_view'
+  | 'grid_select'
+  | 'chiron_toggle'
+  | 'detail_toggle'
+  | 'chart_name_set'
+  | 'comm_read_view'
+  | 'race_view'
+  | 'team_join'
+  | 'weekly_checkin'
+  | 'share_card'
+  | 'trophy_view'
+  | 'season_result_view'
+  | 'trophy_hall_view'
+  | 'race_to_astrofolio'
+  | 'ramp_click';
+export type AnalyticsPropertyValue = string | number | boolean;
+export type AnalyticsProperties = Record<string, AnalyticsPropertyValue>;
+
+export function sanitizeAnalyticsProperties(
+  name: string,
+  properties: Record<string, unknown> = {},
+): AnalyticsProperties | null {
+  const allowed = (ANALYTICS_EVENT_PROPS as Record<string, readonly string[]>)[name];
+  if (!allowed) return null;
+
+  const safe: AnalyticsProperties = {};
+  for (const key of allowed) {
+    const value = properties[key];
+    const values = (ANALYTICS_EVENT_VALUES as Record<
+      string,
+      Readonly<Record<string, readonly string[]>>
+    >)[name]?.[key];
+    if (values && (typeof value !== 'string' || !values.includes(value))) continue;
+    if (typeof value === 'number' || typeof value === 'boolean') safe[key] = value;
+    if (typeof value === 'string' && value.length <= 32) safe[key] = value;
+  }
+  return safe;
+}
+
+export function trackAnalytics(
+  name: AnalyticsEventName,
+  properties: AnalyticsProperties = {},
+): void {
+  if (typeof window === 'undefined') return;
+  const safe = sanitizeAnalyticsProperties(name, properties);
+  if (!safe) return;
+  const analytics = (window as Window & {
+    zodiacsAnalytics?: { track?: (event: string, props: AnalyticsProperties) => void };
+  }).zodiacsAnalytics;
+  analytics?.track?.(name, safe);
+}

+on:

+  # must receive the same regression gates as main.

+  workflow_dispatch:
+    inputs:

+        type: string
+
+permissions:
+  contents: read

+jobs:

+        uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4.4.0
+        with:
+          node-version: 22
+          cache: npm
+
+      - name: Phase 1 protected-scope guard
+        env:
+          PHASE1_SCOPE_BASE: ${{ github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.scope_base || github.event.pull_request.base.sha || github.event.before }}
+        run: npm run test:phase1:scope
+
+      - name: Install
+        run: npm ci
+
+      - name: Dependency advisories stay at zero
+        # Production tree must be clean at any severity; the full tree
+        # (dev included) fails only on high/critical so a low-severity
+        # transitive dev advisory cannot block an unrelated deploy.
+        # Retry only recognized, findings-free audit endpoint outages;
+        # every other failure and exhausted retries remain fatal.
+        run: |
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --omit=dev
+          node scripts/audit-with-retry.mjs --audit-level=high
+
+      - name: Install pinned Chromium
+        run: npx playwright-core install chromium
+
+      - name: Validate registry JSON
+        run: node -e "JSON.parse(require('node:fs').readFileSync('public/registry/zodiacs.registry.json', 'utf8'))"

+          ! grep -RInE 'Symbiosis|ZodiacS(DK)|diasmal[[:digit:]]{3}|zodiacs-org/sdk' public/sdk public/registry README.md CLAUDE.md DESIGNER_HANDOFF.md

+      - name: Wing language stays in the wing

+        # MDX, JSON, email/share code, and API output. Legal and Registry
+        # carve-outs are exact and tested; arbitrary directory bypasses are not.

+
+      - name: Voice — banned tells stay out of the copy

+        # over every content file and template the agents touch.
+        run: |
+          ! grep -RIniE 'done properly|computed properly|shows? (its|their) work|like a human( wrote it)?|no mush|not vibes|speaks human|in plain language|como es debido|sin paja' src/content src/pages src/components src/islands

+      - name: Authorship stays transparent

+# A04 next prerequisite: reference positions must not certify a whole date
+
+**Recommend a conservative reference-only confidence policy for unknown-time calculations.** Keep C-014's admitted reference chart, receipt, positions and ordinary actions. Stop promoting endpoint samples into a verified Moon candidate set or a singular unknown-time Sun record. Reuse the existing unverified Moon presentation contract; do not add a provider, polyfill, runtime requirement or sampling theorem. This is a preparation recommendation, not an implemented change or complete A04 signoff.
+
+## Two current, executed counterexamples
+
+The exact current Moon lookup closure and the exact ChartCalculator calculation/receipt/certainty statement block were extracted with TypeScript AST, bundled with the actual resolver, C-014 membership helper, rc.6 engine/receipt code and actual trust/presentation consumers, then executed under Node 22.23.2 and Chrome 152.0.7977.83. All fifty source/dependency identities remain unchanged. The surrounding state setters and current-run predicate are controlled. This is actual caller-code execution, not an actual product DOM or independent astronomical oracle claim. Translation compiles with the normal server catalog branch for this non-DOM harness.
+
+| Requested unknown-time date | C-014 admitted reference | Current outcome | Actual contradictory member |
+| --- | --- | --- | --- |
+| 1919-03-31, America/Toronto | 1919-03-31 16:00Z, local noon | Chart candidates `[aries]`; Moon lookup shows Aries only; ChartContext marks Moon `established` | 04:30Z formats to local March31 00:30 and passes membership, with Moon **359.71450035822477° Pisces**. 04:29:59.999Z is a nonmember. |
+| 1867-10-18, America/Juneau | 1867-10-17 20:57:41Z, local noon | Chart candidates `[gemini]`; Moon lookup shows Gemini only; ChartContext marks Moon `established` | 1867-10-19 00:31:13Z formats to local October18 15:33:32 and passes membership, with Moon **97.12696569323725° Cancer**. One second earlier is a nonmember. |
+
+These witnesses disprove the candidate claims without requiring a complete date model. Toronto loses the partial-midnight gap's first half-hour; Juneau loses a returned segment after the date-line reversal. Both reference instants remain valid members, so the point witness intentionally does not reject these requests. The engine's positions are not shown to be wrong; their promotion to a complete birth-date statement is wrong.
+
+The actual consequences extend beyond a caption. Toronto's `approachRead` returns Aries-specific Moon trust advice and `chartSignature` chooses “Moon trine Neptune.” An in-memory copy with the same numerical chart but `moonSignCandidates: []` becomes unresolved in `buildChartContext`, returns no Moon-specific trust advice, and chooses a non-Moon signature. Juneau's Gemini-specific Moon advice is likewise removed. An ordinary Bangkok singleton also becomes unverified under this policy: that reduction in claimed certainty is intentional, not a numerical regression.
+
+Nine date controls include the two omissions, the preceding Toronto date, both St Johns return/disconnection dates, repeated Apia, ordinary Bangkok, short New York, and skipped Apia. St Johns and repeated Apia retain their finite observed signs; no missing sign is claimed there. Skipped Apia is still rejected by C-014 before a result. Three explicit-time controls retain success and established point Moon behavior, including shifted known-time Apia. Four finite UTC phase controls show the actual lite phase category changes within January9, January16 and April7 2024, while January1 is a stable control. Consequently the existing Moon copy “phase is unaffected” / “exact from the date alone” is also demonstrably false as a date-wide claim.
+
+## Policy choices
+
+1. **Caption-only disclaimer:** change “exact”/“changed” prose while leaving endpoint singleton metadata authoritative. Small, but insufficient. The executed trust/interpretation consumers still receive `established` and emit sign-specific advice. Reject as the chart correction; a visible reference label alone does not change confidence.
+2. **Reference-only unknown-time confidence (recommended):** preserve the existing admitted reference calculation and portable envelope exactly; withhold verified Moon candidates for unknown time using the existing empty/absent candidate state, and do not infer the singular unknown-time Sun bridge from endpoints. Use wording that says the Moon sign across the date is unverified, not that it necessarily changed. For MoonPhaseTool, display the retained phase/illumination/longitude as a reference result with a visible qualifier, and cease presenting the two endpoint signs as an exhaustive birth-sign choice. A known clock retains existing point behavior. The existing no-time chart/receipt functionality and ownership fences remain available under Node22/Chrome with no interval provider. This trades some previously asserted ordinary-date certainty for truthful coverage.
+3. **Explicit observed-sign metadata:** retain samples as an explicitly incomplete set of observations, separately from verified candidates; never route them through singleton `established` trust. This can retain useful sample information, but needs a new distinction across hero cards, context, advice, signature, scene and share presentation, plus reference labels. It is a larger migration than option2 and still does not prove whole-date completeness. A denser sample, union with noon, two-midnight fix or blacklist of these dates would not provide the missing guarantee.
+
+No false Sun sign was demonstrated by these finite controls. Suppressing the unknown-time singular Sun bridge is a conservative response to its currently unproved coverage assertion, not a claim that these particular Sun positions are wrong. If root keeps that branch temporarily, the remaining unverified Sun inference must stay explicitly open; this preparation does not certify it. No Registry-wing source or ownership SDK change is necessary for a caller-side gate.
+
+## Concrete bounded implementation scope for root to choose
+
+The smallest first release slice for option2 is **ChartCalculator confidence**, owning `src/islands/ChartCalculator.tsx` plus the six `src/lib/i18n/ui/{en,es,fr,it,pt,ru}.ts` catalogs for a dedicated unverified notice. Its unknown-time branch must not populate verified candidates from `moonCandidatesFromEndpoints`, and must not reuse the current “Moon changed signs / both neighbors” copy for an unverified result. Remove unnecessary endpoint work only when no confidence consumer remains. Known-time, local reference/receipt calculation, wheel, save/share formats, typed inputs, ownership fences and numerical values remain unchanged. Existing `moonCandidates`/`buildChartContext`/`approachRead`/signature handling already support the unverified state, as exercised by the policy copy; no new Chart/SDK schema is required. Add focused actual caller/consumer regressions and update the existing Registry-bridge expectation plus relevant unknown-time caller acceptance expectations. `chart-date-certainty.ts` must not retain an advertised “provably stable” claim if it remains a supported endpoint-observation helper; any comment/contract cleanup should be explicit, not silently broaden its algorithm.
+
+The coordinated **Moon reference-label slice** owns `src/islands/MoonPhaseTool.tsx`, the same six catalogs, and the six existing `src/pages/{,es/,fr/,it/,pt/,ru/}moon-phase/index.astro` tool-page copies where date-alone phase exactness is asserted. It needs a result-level unknown/reference distinction (or truthful captured caption), visible for all unknown-time results. A local result must not fabricate an exact noon clock if resolution moved it; a reference-within-the-selected-date statement is guaranteed by C-014 and is sufficient. Preserve no-city explicit UTC and known-time behavior. Remove unsupported exhaustive alternate-sign presentation, and correct the phase invariance claim. No global layout, CSS, navigation, Learn/sign-guide, SDK, API, profile format or provider changes are needed. Root can split these into reviewable releases, but the first release must not be described as fixing the remaining Moon-tool/copy claims.
+
+Before either implementation is accepted, test the real current callers against Toronto and Juneau, a normal singleton, ordinary two-sign dates, no-city UTC, known time, C-014 rejection/recovery and all existing stale-result fences. Preserve exact numerical/receipt bytes while verifying unknown-time trust/advice no longer claims completeness. Any intended changes to old confidence assertions should be named; do not weaken numerical comparisons or add a tolerance. Complete Sun/Moon date coverage remains a separate algorithm/provider/event-bound task.
+
+## Runtime and evidence limits
+
+Node22 has no native Temporal. Chrome ran the same final bundle twice, once normally and once with Temporal explicitly unavailable; complete outputs were exactly equal apart from the capability field. Both browser contexts made only four aggregate owned GET requests and no external requests or page errors. The two historical omissions and point-preservation policy need no native Temporal, dependency install or provider. No cross-runtime bit-equality guarantee is asserted; raw runtime values remain separate.
+
+No root product/docs, server, SDK, source model, history, dependency or publication state was changed. The initial build failed because metadata paths were resolved against the wrong working directory; corrected `absWorkingDir` addresses the harness path. The next run lacked the compile-time SSR catalog flag; the explicit server catalog branch fixes that non-DOM harness environment. Both original errors/scripts/logs remain. Initial Juneau points were correctly classified as nonmembers; the subsequent exact returned-segment witnesses came from the retained reviewed evidence, not an expanded search or completeness claim. Original finite results and bundle are kept under `initial-finite-run`.
+
+`identity.json`, `final-source-check.json`, `node22-result.json`, `browser-result.json`, the exact extraction/harness and `summary.json` contain the executable evidence. The root's separate normal-build/24-page acceptance and independent reviews are not claimed as this preparation's executions.

+# Executed baseline controls before C-015 freeze
+
+The f803 baseline was exercised in actual Chrome 152 with Node 22.23.2, actual Preact/Chart and rc.6 calculation/receipt code. The identity records 211 real source/dependency inputs and three declared transformations: Chart import gates plus pass-through resolver and endpoint counters. No moving candidate was tested.
+
+Fifteen controls passed in the first execution. The two actual-local-save controls stopped before persistence because the reviewer's `.invalid` HTTP fixture origin was not a secure context and native `crypto.randomUUID` was undefined. A separate two-origin browser probe confirms the precise difference: insecure `.invalid` has no randomUUID, while the otherwise identical loopback origin is secure and supplies the native function. The driver changed only to loopback and added an affected-case filter; both local-save controls then passed. The original driver, full result and failure logs remain unmodified. Thus there are seventeen accepted baseline controls drawn from two executions, with two original reviewer-fixture failures retained. No product/auth defect or permission bypass is inferred.
+
+The ordinary unknown-time New York case currently makes one endpoint helper call and two direct `computeBodies` endpoint calls, then exposes a Pisces Moon and Gemini Registry bridge. That is a concrete observation of prior behavior, not evidence that this particular Sun or Moon is false. C-015 is expected to withdraw unproven confidence while preserving its computed reference and receipt. The independent child supplies the distinct historical Moon counterexamples.
+
+The ten primary controls cover New York known/unknown time, Bangkok leap day, Paris seconds offsets, Manaus, a long Apia reference, unknown/known exact pole, signed-offset fallback and Chart moon mode. The baseline captures pre-augmentation chart JSON, the committed numerical fields, optional immutable envelope JSON, direct call sequence and Registry context. Known-pole and signed-offset controls legitimately use the existing legacy calculation without a receipt. The native Blob download exactly matches the captured immutable Paris receipt bytes. Replacement during a delayed receipt-module load computes only the latest input. Editing a known result clears its Registry bridge before an unknown replacement. The existing skipped-date safeguard rejects before primary/receipt/endpoint work, and public positions imports call none of those operations.
+
+Each corrected local-save control executes the actual legacy store exactly once in a disposable context. Birth input, saved summary and emitted reference-Sun context are retained for frozen-candidate comparison. IDs and timestamps are naturally generated; equality will compare the stable birth/summary fields, not those incidental values. This preserves a local write contract and does not certify real account authority, backend synchronization, whole-date Sun confidence or reversible cancellation of already requested writes.
+
+Candidate acceptance remains pending the author's immutable freeze. All files here belong to the review scratch; no root, author, source repository, SDK, remote service or shared platform document was modified.

+# C-015 independent preservation review preparation
+
+Base: `f803d2543ad81343b22d49326b8b46d0e2ea03a0`. Product source is an immutable private copy of 1,835 files, with a full source manifest. Root remains the integrator; the author supplies a frozen patch later. No moving author source is used as acceptance. The separate child is reviewing Toronto/Juneau consumer semantics; this review does not repeat those counterexamples.
+
+The approved narrow policy is sound as a conservative removal of an unsupported confidence inference. The existing `moonCandidates` contract already interprets an explicit empty array as unverified, and `moonIsUncertain` then keeps a lone reference longitude from becoming a settled Moon label. Reusing that contract avoids inventing another public confidence schema or silently making endpoint sampling authoritative again. The `moonAmbiguousNotice` wording must describe missing verification rather than claim an observed sign change; consumer text/reading/share consequences are the child's independent scope.
+
+For unknown time, the primary calculation currently succeeds before Chart calls the date-endpoint helper and two body-position evaluations. It then assigns endpoint Moon candidates and may choose a singular Sun Registry record if the sampled signs agree. Removing those confidence operations should leave primary reference resolution, witness validation, calculation and envelope serialization unchanged. It also avoids rejecting a successfully computed point because a later confidence lookup fails, but no injected failure is an observed IANA/ephemeris defect by itself. Our counters distinguish these two direct endpoint body calls from the actual primary ephemeris work; “zero numerical work” would be false.
+
+The portable helper serializes the envelope before the caller augments presentation metadata. Its returned string is immutable. The review will compare that string byte-for-byte, pre-augmentation chart bytes, and the committed chart's numerical fields after omitting only `moonSignCandidates`. This catches accidental mutation of coordinates, flags, instant, houses, aspects, bodies or provenance. It also covers signed-offset and exact-known-pole legacy paths which legitimately have no portable envelope. The existing optional-module failure and no-recalculation-on-portable-failure rule remain outside this change and must not be weakened.
+
+The singular Sun Registry bridge is a separate actionable claim. Disabling it for every unknown-time input sacrifices some valid links, but preserves the existing known-time path without claiming an observed false Sun. The exact bridge DOM and its impression/click gating must be tested; the sanctioned records cross-link and optional saved-chart Registry Collection path are different code paths. The latter must remain unchanged. Reference-Sun naming, `chart-computed`, post-chart daily context and legacy saved-summary bodies remain as existing, explicitly open product limitations. A hidden Registry link does not settle those broader semantics or stop an already requested save.
+
+Two defensible options were compared:
+
+1. Apply the approved explicit unverified sentinel and remove endpoint confidence calls. It works in existing runtimes, preserves the useful point calculation and receipt, and fails the singular Registry gate conservatively. This is the smallest bounded slice.
+2. Introduce a validated whole-date coverage plus body-extrema/crossing proof before exposing candidates or Registry. Native Temporal availability alone supplies neither all-runtime date coverage nor astronomical candidate completeness; the inactive interval provider cannot by itself justify this. That is a separate algorithm and compatibility policy, not a safer small substitute here.
+
+The independent browser fixture executes actual Preact/Chart, resolver, receipt helper and rc.6 numerical code. Declared boundaries are synthetic city options, import-loader gates, pass-through function-entry counters, and a controlled share-artifact side effect. Its actual local save and native Blob download occur only in disposable offline contexts. It is not a full Astro page, production import graph, real account/backend or independent ephemeris oracle.
+
+The prepared baseline matrix covers ordinary New York known/unknown time, Bangkok leap day, Paris historical seconds, Manaus, long Apia reference, unknown/known exact pole, signed-offset fallback and Chart moon mode. Additional actual-caller controls cover the existing local save for known/unknown time, exact Blob receipt bytes, replacement while receipt loading is pending, known-to-unknown Registry clearing, skipped-date refusal before primary work and public positions-only initialization. Baseline observations of a visible unknown-time Registry link are evidence of prior behavior, not a reproduced false-Sun claim. The frozen candidate must match the relevant numerical/envelope/save fields while changing only declared confidence output and gating.
+
+Source review will independently compare primary calculation/capture, ownership/ref/export, save-call, context publication and Registry-rendering paths; the only allowed semantic delta in the calculation is replacement of endpoint-derived confidence. It will also confirm that `chart-date-certainty` changes are comment-only and that package/SDK/Moon tool/fixed-noon/phase-at-birth surfaces are untouched. Existing global/localized styles must remain unchanged.
+
+Preparation command/path errors are retained separately. This document is review preparation, not acceptance of an unfrozen candidate.

+# Executed baseline controls before C-015 freeze
+
+The f803 baseline was exercised in actual Chrome 152 with Node 22.23.2, actual Preact/Chart and rc.6 calculation/receipt code. The identity records 211 real source/dependency inputs and three declared transformations: Chart import gates plus pass-through resolver and endpoint counters. No moving candidate was tested.
+
+Fifteen controls passed in the first execution. The two actual-local-save controls stopped before persistence because the reviewer's `.invalid` HTTP fixture origin was not a secure context and native `crypto.randomUUID` was undefined. A separate two-origin browser probe confirms the precise difference: insecure `.invalid` has no randomUUID, while the otherwise identical loopback origin is secure and supplies the native function. The driver changed only to loopback and added an affected-case filter; both local-save controls then passed. The original driver, full result and failure logs remain unmodified. Thus there are seventeen accepted baseline controls drawn from two executions, with two original reviewer-fixture failures retained. No product/auth defect or permission bypass is inferred.
+
+The ordinary unknown-time New York case currently makes one endpoint helper call and two direct `computeBodies` endpoint calls, then exposes a Pisces Moon and Gemini Registry bridge. That is a concrete observation of prior behavior, not evidence that this particular Sun or Moon is false. C-015 is expected to withdraw unproven confidence while preserving its computed reference and receipt. The independent child supplies the distinct historical Moon counterexamples.
+
+The ten primary controls cover New York known/unknown time, Bangkok leap day, Paris seconds offsets, Manaus, a long Apia reference, unknown/known exact pole, signed-offset fallback and Chart moon mode. The baseline captures pre-augmentation chart JSON, the committed numerical fields, optional immutable envelope JSON, direct call sequence and Registry context. Known-pole and signed-offset controls legitimately use the existing legacy calculation without a receipt. The native Blob download exactly matches the captured immutable Paris receipt bytes. Replacement during a delayed receipt-module load computes only the latest input. Editing a known result clears its Registry bridge before an unknown replacement. The existing skipped-date safeguard rejects before primary/receipt/endpoint work, and public positions imports call none of those operations.
+
+Each corrected local-save control executes the actual legacy store exactly once in a disposable context. Birth input, saved summary and emitted reference-Sun context are retained for frozen-candidate comparison. IDs and timestamps are naturally generated; equality will compare the stable birth/summary fields, not those incidental values. This preserves a local write contract and does not certify real account authority, backend synchronization, whole-date Sun confidence or reversible cancellation of already requested writes.
+
+Candidate acceptance remains pending the author's immutable freeze. All files here belong to the review scratch; no root, author, source repository, SDK, remote service or shared platform document was modified.

+# C-015 independent preservation review preparation
+
+Base: `f803d2543ad81343b22d49326b8b46d0e2ea03a0`. Product source is an immutable private copy of 1,835 files, with a full source manifest. Root remains the integrator; the author supplies a frozen patch later. No moving author source is used as acceptance. The separate child is reviewing Toronto/Juneau consumer semantics; this review does not repeat those counterexamples.
+
+The approved narrow policy is sound as a conservative removal of an unsupported confidence inference. The existing `moonCandidates` contract already interprets an explicit empty array as unverified, and `moonIsUncertain` then keeps a lone reference longitude from becoming a settled Moon label. Reusing that contract avoids inventing another public confidence schema or silently making endpoint sampling authoritative again. The `moonAmbiguousNotice` wording must describe missing verification rather than claim an observed sign change; consumer text/reading/share consequences are the child's independent scope.
+
+For unknown time, the primary calculation currently succeeds before Chart calls the date-endpoint helper and two body-position evaluations. It then assigns endpoint Moon candidates and may choose a singular Sun Registry record if the sampled signs agree. Removing those confidence operations should leave primary reference resolution, witness validation, calculation and envelope serialization unchanged. It also avoids rejecting a successfully computed point because a later confidence lookup fails, but no injected failure is an observed IANA/ephemeris defect by itself. Our counters distinguish these two direct endpoint body calls from the actual primary ephemeris work; “zero numerical work” would be false.
+
+The portable helper serializes the envelope before the caller augments presentation metadata. Its returned string is immutable. The review will compare that string byte-for-byte, pre-augmentation chart bytes, and the committed chart's numerical fields after omitting only `moonSignCandidates`. This catches accidental mutation of coordinates, flags, instant, houses, aspects, bodies or provenance. It also covers signed-offset and exact-known-pole legacy paths which legitimately have no portable envelope. The existing optional-module failure and no-recalculation-on-portable-failure rule remain outside this change and must not be weakened.
+
+The singular Sun Registry bridge is a separate actionable claim. Disabling it for every unknown-time input sacrifices some valid links, but preserves the existing known-time path without claiming an observed false Sun. The exact bridge DOM and its impression/click gating must be tested; the sanctioned records cross-link and optional saved-chart Registry Collection path are different code paths. The latter must remain unchanged. Reference-Sun naming, `chart-computed`, post-chart daily context and legacy saved-summary bodies remain as existing, explicitly open product limitations. A hidden Registry link does not settle those broader semantics or stop an already requested save.
+
+Two defensible options were compared:
